lines.content: This repository is a starter template for a greenfield Java project used in an introductory software engineering course in an undergraduate computer science program. Students use it as the starting point for their own projects.

Unless the user says otherwise, assume that you are assisting a student working on a project in this repository. If the user identifies themselves as an instructor or another project stakeholder, adapt your response to that role.
* Prior knowledge: Basic Java and OOP concepts.
* IDE and level of expertise: IntelliJ, Beginner
* Explain the rationale for significant actions: what you did and why.
* Keep explanations brief but instructive, supporting learning through responsible use of AI. For example:
* When suggesting a Git command, briefly explain what it does.
* Add explanatory Javadoc comments to all classes and to nontrivial methods and fields when their purpose or behavior is not obvious.
* Make generated code as self-explanatory as possible, and include explanatory comments where they improve understanding.
* When faced with a design choice, choose the simplest option that is sufficient for the requirements, while briefly explaining relevant more advanced alternatives.
All Java code in this project MUST follow the project-specific
This includes package declarations, encapsulation, explicit imports, 4-space indentation,
K&R braces, a maximum line length of 120 characters, and Javadoc for public classes and methods.
Ensure that Java 25 is used when running the application or build tasks. On macOS, use `sdk use java 25.0.3.fx-zulu` to switch to Java 25 if needed.
All future commits and branch names in this project MUST follow the project-specific
Commit subjects must be imperative, capitalized, free of a trailing period, and at most
72 characters. Non-trivial commits must include a blank-line-separated body wrapped at
72 characters explaining what changed and why. Branch names must be meaningful kebab-case.
Use lightweight tags unless the user requests an annotated tag.
When proposing or creating a commit message, include enough detail to explain the rationale for the change.
Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked.

Slowbro is a command-line task manager that helps you keep track of tasks,
Start Slowbro and enter one command at a time. Slowbro saves your task list
automatically, so your tasks remain available the next time you start the
- `<description>`, `<date or time>`, and `<task number>` are values you provide.
- Text inside backticks represents a command or literal keyword.
- Task numbers refer to the numbers shown by `list`.
- Commands must be entered in lowercase.
Use `todo` to add a task without a deadline or time period.
Slowbro adds the task to your list and assigns it a task number.
Use `deadline` to add a task that must be completed by a specific date or
Use `event` to add an activity with a starting and ending time.
Use `list` to display every task in your task list.
Each task is shown with its task number. Use this number when marking or
deleting a task. Task numbers start from `1` and match the numbers displayed by
Use `find` to search for tasks whose descriptions contain a keyword.
The search is case-insensitive and matches keywords anywhere in the task
description. For example, `find assign` also matches `Submit assignment`.
Use `mark` followed by the task number.
### Mark a task as not done
Use `unmark` followed by the task number to change a completed task back to
Use `delete` followed by the task number to remove a task.
> Deleting a task removes it from your task list. Check the task number
- Ensure that every command has the required arguments.
- Do not leave task descriptions, deadlines, or event times empty.
- Use a valid task number shown by `list`.
Slowbro stores your tasks in `data/slowbro.txt` relative to the directory where
the application is run. Do not edit this file manually unless you know the
Slowbro saves your task list automatically whenever you add, update, or delete
a task. No separate save command is required.
| Add deadline | `deadline <description> /by <date or time>` | Add a deadline |
| Mark done | `mark <task number>` | Mark a task as complete |
| Mark not done | `unmark <task number>` | Reopen a task |
| Delete task | `delete <task number>` | Remove a task |
